meta.title: One Asset, Two Clocks
meta.subtitle: The same authored timeline read by a predicted gameplay clock and a frame-based presentation clock — and the clip kind decides which

views.label: One authored asset
views.note: Clips, curves and timestamps bake into a blob that is byte-identical on every machine. Only the start tick travels.

views.label: The predicted clock
views.note: Position is derived, not accumulated: current tick minus start tick. Stateless, so replay costs nothing to undo.

views.label: The presentation clock
views.note: Once per rendered frame, on the client only. It samples the gameplay clock instead of keeping its own sum.

views.label: Four kinds, four homes
views.note: Value clips are pure. Spawn clips route through a predicted spawn request. Authority clips never reach the client prefab.

cards.title: Accumulate versus derive
items: elapsed += deltaTime is a register: its value depends on every previous tick
elapsed = tick − start is combinational: it depends only on the tick
Rollback restores the tick for free, so the derived form needs no save or restore
The shipped package accumulates, at TimerUpdateSystem.cs:475

cards.title: The rollback boundary
items: Rollback restores component values, not entity existence
The backup is a memcopy of ghost components · GhostPredictionHistorySystem.cs:184
An entity spawned during a replayed tick is still there when that tick replays
So spawns are reconciled, not undone, via PredictedGhostSpawnRequest

cards.title: Where the shipped group actually sits
items: PredictedSimulationSystemGroup is a sibling ordered first, not a parent
So the timeline runs after the whole prediction loop, never inside it
Filter is Simulation | Presentation | Editor | Menu · TimelineSystemGroup.cs:20

cards.title: Two rate managers, two shapes of delta
items: Server re-enters SimulationSystemGroup once per tick · NetcodeServerRateManager.cs:48
Client runs it exactly once per rendered frame · NetcodeClientRateManager.cs:54
Client delta lands on a fraction of a tick · NetcodeClientRateManager.cs:108
Nothing replicates or restores the timer, so the gap is never corrected
